0.name: Healthy Sugarcane
0.description: Foliage exhibits vigorous chlorophyll pigmentation, uniform venation, and absence of necrotic lesions or discoloration.
next_steps: Continue scheduled irrigation and balanced NPK nutrition.
Maintain bi-weekly visual inspections during active tillering.
Record observations to preserve historical health baseline.

1.name: Red Rot
1.description: Major fungal vascular disease characterized by red discoloration across leaf midribs, internal stalk reddening with white horizontal patches, and rapid cane drying.
symptoms: Spreading red lesions on leaf midribs
White patches across reddened stalk tissues
next_steps: Isolate and rogue out infected clumps immediately to prevent spore dispersal.
Avoid ratoon cropping in infected patches.
Use certified disease-free setts treated with hot-water (52°C for 30 mins) or Trichoderma viride.
Ensure field drainage to eliminate standing stagnant moisture.

2.name: Sugarcane Mosaic Virus
2.description: Potyvirus transmitted primarily by corn leaf aphids (Rhopalosiphum maidis), resulting in contrasting dark and light green chlorotic mottling on younger leaves.
symptoms: Alternating pale green / yellowish streaks and islands
Chlorotic blotches on expanding spindle leaves
next_steps: Eradicate aphid vectors using biological controls or approved horticultural neem spray.
Rogue out severely stunted stools in nursery plots.
Plant resistant sugarcane cultivars (e.g. Co 86032, Co 0238 where resistant clones exist).

3.name: Leaf Scald
3.description: Vascular bacterial wilt manifesting as sharp, pencil-line white stripes along leaf veins that expand into scalded, bleached foliar necrosis resembling fire scorch.
symptoms: Narrow, sharply defined 'pencil lines' along veins
Inward curling of leaves creating scalded appearance
next_steps: Disinfect harvesting knives and cultivation implements with 10% bleach or Lysol between plots.
Use heat-treated seed setts to eliminate latent vascular bacteria.
Improve drainage and avoid excessive nitrogen application during wet seasons.

4.name: Yellow Leaf Disease
4.description: Aphid-borne luteovirus causing bright yellowing of midribs on leaves 3 to 6 from the top, gradually spreading outward into the lamina and reducing sucrose content.
symptoms: Distinct intense yellowing of midrib lower surface
Reddish-pink discoloration on upper midrib in later stages
next_steps: Deploy tissue-culture derived disease-free planting material.
Monitor and manage vector sugarcane aphid (Melanaphis sacchari) colonies.
Optimize potassium and micronutrient supplementation to alleviate foliar stress.
